source: Triodian project note 'United States - jurisdiction scope (US.1)' and the Atlas US round (data/research/2026-11-14-us-overlay.json in obligations-atlas). Failure cases describe what can go wrong; whether an instrument applies is counsel's question, and the matter brief lists the records.

packs.name: Bank (United States)
packs.instruments: SR 26-2 on model risk, the 2023 interagency third-party guidance (with the September 2026 proposal to replace it) and, in New York, 23 NYCRR 500
failures: A vendor credit or fraud model is put into use without validation, and the people relying on it do not know its limits.
A generative or agentic AI tool is treated as outside model risk management, so nobody owns its testing or monitoring.
An AI provider's subcontractor holds customer data, and the bank's contract gives it no audit right that reaches the subcontractor.
An automated decision about a consumer is made without the notice a state automated-decision law may call for.
redLineCandidates: Generative or agentic AI acting on customer accounts with no owner under the model risk or third-party framework

packs.name: Insurer (United States)
packs.instruments: the NAIC model bulletin on AI systems as each state has issued it and, in New York, Insurance Circular Letter No. 7
failures: An underwriting or pricing model uses external consumer data that acts as a proxy for a protected class, and testing did not find it.
A model vendor will not provide audit reports or cooperate with a regulator's inquiry, and the contract gives the insurer no right to either.
The written AI programme exists on paper, but the board or its committee never receives reports on it.
An automated decision about a consumer is made without the notice a state automated-decision law may call for.
redLineCandidates: An adverse underwriting, pricing or claims decision made by AI that no person can review

packs.name: Broker-dealer or investment adviser (United States)
packs.instruments: Regulation S-P, FINRA Rule 3110 and FINRA's 2026 report on generative AI and AI agents
failures: An AI agent takes actions for a customer beyond the scope its supervisors approved.
A generative AI tool used by registered staff sits outside the firm's written supervisory procedures.
An AI provider holding customer information has a breach and does not tell the firm within the 72 hours its contract sets.
Communications drafted by AI go to customers without the review the firm applies to other communications.
redLineCandidates: An AI agent placing trades or moving customer assets outside a scope a supervisor has approved

packs.name: Health care provider (United States)
packs.instruments: 45 CFR 92.210 on patient care decision support tools, the HIPAA business associate terms and the HTI-5 changes to certified health IT
failures: A clinical decision support tool uses race, sex, age or disability as an input, and nobody identified or reduced the risk of discrimination.
An AI scribe or assistant processes patient records with no business associate agreement in place.
A predictive tool inside the electronic health record changes, and the vendor no longer supplies its source or known limits.
Patients are not told that AI is used in their care where a state law calls for that disclosure.
redLineCandidates: AI deciding to deny or delay a patient's care with no clinician reviewing it

packs.name: Critical infrastructure owner or operator (United States)
packs.instruments: NERC CIP-013 supply chain risk management (bulk electric system) and CIRCIA incident and ransom-payment reporting once its final rule is in force
failures: An AI tool with remote access to operational systems is bought without the supply chain controls set for other vendors.
A cyber incident that involves an AI system or provider is not recognised as reportable, and the reporting window is missed.
An AI agent changes an operational technology setting with no authorised person approving the change.
redLineCandidates: AI changing a safety-critical operational setting with no authorised person approving it
